## Combining the evidence {.title-slide-custom}

<p class="subtitle">A closer look at the <em>TNNT2</em> p.Asp259Ala example</p>

<p class="byline">Shaurita D. Hutchins</p>

<img class="title-logo nostretch" src="../assets/images/cfde.svg"
alt="CFDE Training Center">

## What the paper reports

- **Gene:** *TNNT2*
- **Variant:** c.776A&gt;C, p.Asp259Ala
- **Study classification:** variant of uncertain significance
- **Cohort evidence:** Two other participants with DCM carried pathogenic or
  likely pathogenic *TNNT2* variants

These findings support the relevance of *TNNT2* to DCM in this cohort.

<p class="source-note">Source: Linnér et al. 2025,
<a href="https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-88465-8">Supplementary Table S4</a>.</p>

## *TNNT2* expression and protein information

- **GTEx:** Median expression of 2,896.66 TPM in left ventricle
- **HuBMAP:** Expression above zero in 38.2% of the retrieved ventricular
  cardiac-myocyte records
- **Pharos:** Tbio with 441 publications and 167 protein-interaction records

This evidence supports using cardiac myocytes as a model to study the variant.

<p class="source-note">Sources:
<a href="https://gtexportal.org/api/v2/docs">GTEx Portal API</a>,
<a href="https://docs.hubmapconsortium.org/apis.html">HuBMAP APIs</a>, and
<a href="https://pharos.nih.gov/api">Pharos API</a>.</p>

## ProtVar supports testing thin-filament function

::: {.prediction-table}
| Source/Tool | Prediction | What it describes |
|---|---|---|
| AlphaMissense | Pathogenic, 0.8296 | Variant-effect prediction |
| EVE | Uncertain, 0.575 | Evolutionary model |
| FoldX | −0.369 kcal/mol | Protein stability estimate |
| AlphaFold | pLDDT 92.88 | Confidence in predicted structure |
:::

<br>

- Cardiac troponin T interacts with troponin I, troponin C, and tropomyosin to
regulate thin-filament contraction.
- Compare wild-type and p.Asp259Ala troponin complexes across calcium concentrations.
- Measure calcium sensitivity and maximum thin-filament activation.

The variant remains a variant of uncertain significance.

<p class="source-note">Source:
<a href="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ProtVar/api/swagger-ui/index.html">ProtVar API</a>.</p>

## Questions for another candidate genetic variant

1. What did the source study report?
2. Is the gene expressed in the relevant tissue and cell type?
3. What is known about the protein and variant?
4. Which experiment could test the predicted effect?
